- Model consistently underestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially in the first 5–10 days of the 30-day window.
- Forecast tends to overshoot after sharp price spikes (e.g., 79+), then corrects downward — model lags in recognizing the peak and overreacts to subsequent decline.
- Mean reversion is not captured: model fails to anticipate gradual decline after peaks, often holding high forecasts longer than actual price behavior.
- Forecast bias is downward in the latter half of the 30-day window — model systematically underpredicts prices after mid-period.
- Model exhibits “late correction” bias: overestimates early decline, then underestimates later recovery — especially around day 20–25.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in the first 10 days, then overly pessimistic in the last 10 days — model fails to adjust for seasonal or trend-based momentum.
